self_harm.detail: Cut himself in high school. Heaviest at age 15-16. Scars on arm AND stomach. Started cutting near other scars to hide it. Multiple drivers braided together: (1) controlling pain on his terms, (2) 'life force spilling out,' (3) knowing it would hurt his parents if they saw it — a message, not just an act, (4) anger at the world and everything around him. Trigger context: CJ had gone to a different school, so Shawn was isolated; he was facing the realization he was NOT going to be a wrestler and that the accident would impact him long-term. It stopped when peer reaction outweighed the relief — 'too much flak from people around me that wasn't worth the value I was getting from it.'

management_philosophy.detail: Took the playbook from Elon Musk at Quorum: leave meetings that waste your time, call people out who aren't contributing, chew through ineffective resources, jump in and do the work yourself when others can't deliver. Anchor story: one Quorum engineer spent 300 hours on a data-import project Shawn had estimated at 30 (being generous) — Shawn came in and did most of it in 8. Went through 'more than a dozen' Quorum resources — some they thought were top resources — and 'chewed them up and spit them out.' Three-stage arc of self-reflection on this era: regret (Session 5d) → softening (Session 6, 'should have been more collaborative') → vindication (2026-05-13, 'AI now proves the playbook was right; the environment was wrong'). EnergiAcres / Terrasow is the org being built on the Read-2 playbook: AI strips the bullshit so engineers can show what they actually do.

DAILY 5 (2026-08-02) — WAKING UP IN THE ICU: Shawn woke a couple days after the accident in the ICU. It was the first time he'd ever been kept OVERNIGHT in a hospital that he remembers — but he already knew the place: familiar with emergency rooms, monitors, the whole environment. He knew where he was and tried to go back to sleep. He woke again, looked at the monitors, went back to sleep — telling himself that if he just kept sleeping he'd wake up and be home. The devastating realization: there was no going home. THE HOSPITAL WAS HIS HOME. (Shawn) [Standalone-piece candidate — Fractured.]

DAILY 5 (2026-08-02) — THE GANGRENE REVEAL (continues the ICU scene): Eventually Shawn started calling out for help; a nurse came right over. His parents had gone home and had to be called back — a couple hours' drive. Later that same day the doctors removed his bandages to see what the wound looked like. When they pulled the bandages off — with his parents now in the room — the stench filled the room: rotting flesh. GANGRENE had set in. A disgusting sight. (Shawn) [Pairs with the ICU 'hospital was home' beat and the earlier surgery/gamifying material — Fractured.]

DAILY 5 (2026-08-02) — SELF-MEDICATION THREAD (flagged for the book): With so many surgeries, Shawn needed something to look forward to — and that became the painkillers. He'd take whatever was prescribed and enjoy it. THE DEBRIDEMENT: surgeries seemed to come every other day to cut away the dead, rotting flesh; between them they used WET-TO-DRY dressings — put wet gauze on, let it dry (or mostly dry), then RIP it off, tearing the rotting flesh away with it, before going back in to cut more. The pain was so severe he would pass out, and he was put on a MORPHINE DRIP. He admits he came to like morphine and the opioids, and experienced 'all forms of those over the years.' Shawn names this openly as a self-medication throughline that will be part of the book. (Shawn) [Sensitive; record faithfully — Fractured.]

DAILY 5 (2026-08-02) — ACCIDENT DAY, THE SETUP + THE SPEED IRONY: A normal fall school day — went to school, played football outside. Shawn was on the SOCCER team only because he'd gotten in trouble and was stuck on the 'green bench' at lunch; the deal was, agree to play soccer and get off the bench, so he did. The team almost won the championship that year; Shawn played GOALIE — chosen not to avoid running but because he got to wear the cool gloves and a cool/different keeper shirt. THE IRONY: he was actually the FASTEST kid in the class — in fact the fastest in the whole SCHOOL at outdoor field day, where as a 4TH-GRADER he beat every SIXTH-GRADER (sixth grade was CJ's class). Speed was his forte and he worked at it. Sets up the tragedy: the fastest kid, about to be maimed on a machine. (Shawn)

DAILY 5 (2026-08-02) — THE BUS & THE DRIVEWAY (accident day): On the bus ride home Shawn and CJ talked about getting the gas — hyped up about riding a four-wheeler to go pick it up so they'd have gas for the four-wheelers. Walking up the driveway, CJ went into 'coaching' mode: 'why don't you go do it yourself?' Shawn, thrilled at the chance to drive the BIG four-wheeler he didn't usually get to drive alone, took it on — 'I was on it.' Corroborates the Session 8 account of CJ as the salesman who set the day in motion. (Shawn)

DAILY 5 (2026-08-02) — THE WEEK THAT WAS SUPPOSED TO BE GREAT (accident timing): Shawn was in FIFTH GRADE. The week was just getting started — Tuesday was gas day, which set them up for the week. He had a soccer PIZZA PARTY the next day. And it was HALLOWEEN, his favorite holiday — dressing up, candy. He remembers how much he was looking forward to all of it: 'this was gonna be a good week.' THE CLOSER: 'There was no candy that year.' The accident took Halloween and the whole good week with it. (Shawn) [Grade note: field-day speed story was 4th grade; the accident was 5th grade / age ~10-11, around Halloween 1990 — reconcile with the 1990-10-29 date on file.]

DAILY 5 (2026-08-02) — THE CHAIN OF SMALL DELAYS (accident mechanics + meaning): Shawn rode the 125cc Honda four-wheeler with the wagon and empty gas cans to BORMAN'S to pick up gas. The WAGON FELL OFF — he had to go get a bolt to reattach it, costing an extra ~15 minutes. At Borman's he COULDN'T fill the tanks (gas wasn't there; they said it'd be delivered the next day), so he had to drop the wagon and leave it there rather than haul an empty wagon home — and would have to come back the next day anyway. Each little thing — a few minutes here, a few seconds there — is what put him on that road at that exact moment. THE McDONALD'S PIECE: on the drive out it clicked why CJ pushed him to go alone — CJ knew Mom was coming home to take them into town, maybe for McDonald's, so Shawn had a reason to GO FAST. THE MEANING: Shawn frames it as the origin of everything — 'if it wasn't for that, I wouldn't have gotten into computers, into technology; it wouldn't be so intellectual. I wouldn't have been the one who traced out every frame of his memory to figure out why I ended up on that road at that time.' The accident made him the systems-thinker who reconstructs causal chains. (Shawn)

physical.description:
Built thick — stocky, broad shoulders, barrel chest, thick forearms, hairy chest. Approximately 5'10"–5'11" (Session 6 confirmation). Dark brown hair throughout life — long and shaggy in his teens (high-school graduation photo: shoulder-length brown hair, big smile, no mustache yet, cap and gown on a football field, ~1974), still long for his wedding to Beth (white tuxedo with black satin lapels, ruffled shirt, black bowtie, pink boutonniere, thin mustache just coming in). After that, the hair gets cut short and lives under a ball cap for the rest of his life — he was ashamed of going bald and hid it under the hat (Shawn trained himself to own it instead). The signature feature is the thick dark mustache, going gray by his late forties. Greenish-hazel eyes that stuck out — the eyes Shawn inherited. Strong jaw, prominent brow, thick neck. Tanned and weathered from oilfield work and, later, Florida sun. Big thick hands.

Uniform: a ball cap (the iconic pink 'Cutter Oil Co.' cap with the pump-jack logo, or the black Cutter Oil cap, or the yellow Cutter Oil cap, or a generic red cap — almost never without one). White cotton t-shirt or sleeveless cutoff, Marlboros in the breast pocket. Gold chain visible at the collar (sometimes with a pendant). Sunglasses hung off the neckline of a tank top. Jeans and work boots. Carhartt in winter.
